$comment: TEMPLATE — INERT AS SHIPPED. Read policy/README.md first.
Every key below must be verified against YOUR installed binary before it is relied upon.
A misspelled or removed key silently does nothing, which looks identical to working.
Enable one key at a time and run the doctor after each.
Keys are grouped by what they buy. Nothing here is a security boundary except the sandbox.

sandbox.$comment: Without failIfUnavailable a missing backend degrades to zero enforcement, silently.
sandbox.$comment_excluded: Keep empty. This array merges from every scope and cannot be locked down; hash-check the resolved list at SessionStart. Detection only.

permissions.$comment_paths: A single leading slash is NOT absolute — it anchors to the settings source. Absolute requires a double slash. Write(), NotebookEdit() and Glob() rules are accepted but never match; use Edit() and Read().
permissions.$comment_scope: Never write a bare tool name here unless you intend to remove the tool from the model's context entirely — a bare name invalidates the prompt cache.

permissions.$comment: permissions.ask is the ONLY mechanism that forces a human prompt in every mode. Everything else runs silent. Keep this list short — it is the whole nag budget. Never use a bare Bash ask rule; it is substituted away when sandboxing is on and your gate silently stops prompting.

$4_silence.$comment: Keep the away-summary and recap enabled — they are the built-in zero-nag re-entry affordance and a competing digest would be redundant.

$5_remove_competing_authorities.$comment_memory: Keyed on the git repo, so every worktree session writes into one truncation-limited file; re-injected after compaction so it outlives our context; never loaded into subagents.
$5_remove_competing_authorities.$comment_claudemd: All discovered CLAUDE.md files are CONCATENATED, not overridden, and contradictory rules are resolved arbitrarily. One past install of an unrelated tool can silently contradict this project everywhere on the machine.
$5_remove_competing_authorities.$comment_git: Removes a system-prompt-level competitor to our worktree discipline. Does not block git — pair with the pre-tool gate.

$6_fuses_for_unattended_work.$comment: Verify names and value types against your binary; several of these are documented as strings rather than booleans, and spawn-depth defaults have changed without a migration notice.

$7_worktrees.$comment: Set explicitly. The default flipped back to branching from the remote default, which silently drops unpushed commits from new worktrees.

$8_the_enforcement_spine.$comment: Managed-scope hooks are the copy that survives lower-scope configuration. The plugin ships behaviour; policy ships the guarantee. Point these at root-owned scripts OUTSIDE the plugin root, which is user-writable and changes path on every update.
